methodological_rigor.justification: The study leverages the prospective DECIDER trial (NCT04846933) with WGS from 219 treatment-naive tumor samples across 66 patients in two independent cohorts, complemented by LDI-PCR/Nanopore long-read sequencing for orthogonal L1 insertion detection, cell line retrotransposition reporter assays (PA-1 with LRE3 WT/RT-/rs201455670 variant), scRNA-seq, miRNA qRT-PCR, IHC for L1-ORF1p and Ki67, and functional LIN28 inhibitor (C1632) experiments. Rigorous bioinformatic pipelines (BWA-MEM, Mutect2, GATK, xTea, ASCAT, SigProfiler, ovaHRDscar) are used. L1 burden was replicated in two independent cohorts. Some cohorts have modest per-group sample sizes (n=30 L1-high, n=29 L1-low).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an observational cohort study with prospective clinical data collection (DECIDER trial) of HGSC patients with multi-region tumor sampling and longitudinal analyses - Oxford LoE 2b (individual cohort study). Clinical relevance is strong: identifying L1 retrotransposition as a driver of intrapatient heterogeneity with associations to proliferation vs immune/death pathways suggests retrotransposition-associated DNA damage or replication stress as a molecular vulnerability for precision oncology, informing future therapeutic targeting.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are thorough with RRID identifiers for cell lines, antibodies, and software tools throughout; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT04846933) reported; informed consent referenced (text REDACTED for ethics approval number). Supplementary tables for primers and cycling conditions. Reanalysis of WGS data with specified tool versions (Trimmomatic 0.32, BWA-MEM 0.7.12, Mutect2, ASCAT). Software versions and accession databases explicitly cited. Cohort stratification rules defined. Consistent with STROBE for observational design.

novelty_literature.justification: First systematic multi-region quantification of L1 retrotransposition contribution to intrapatient heterogeneity in HGSC, showing L1 profiles diverge more between sites than SNV profiles. Identification of a specific ORF2p inactivating variant (rs201455670) in RC-L1_22q12.1 and functional LIN28 inhibitor validation link molecular determinants of retrotransposition competence. Conceptual advance that L1 retrotransposition is ongoing/late-stage process shaping tumor evolution beyond being passenger events.

writing_presentation.justification: Abstract duplicated (likely formatting artifact). Methods section is extremely detailed with reagent sources and versioning. Logical structure: detection method validation -> cohort-level L1 burden -> transcriptomic correlates -> molecular mechanisms -> intrapatient heterogeneity. Appropriate use of supplementary tables for dense technical content. Overall well-written and appropriate for a specialist audience.

key_strengths: Two independent HGSC cohorts (28 and 38 patients, 219 tumor samples) from prospective DECIDER trial with multi-region sampling enabling intrapatient heterogeneity analysis
Orthogonal L1 detection combining short-read WGS (xTea) and LDI-PCR long-read Nanopore sequencing for high-confidence insertion calling
Functional validation of candidate inactivating ORF2p variant (rs201455670) using LRE3 L1 reporter retrotransposition assay in PA-1 cells
Integration of transcriptomics (cancer-cell-specific via PRISM), scRNA-seq, miRNA analysis, and IHC/IF for comprehensive molecular characterization
LIN28 inhibitor (C1632) functional assay connecting let-7/LIN28 axis to L1 retrotransposition mechanistically
key_concerns: Stratification into L1-high vs L1-low by quartiles may be underpowered at the patient level (combined cohorts but subgroups remain modest)
Abstract duplication appears to be a formatting error from manuscript conversion
Functional implications for precision oncology remain speculative - no direct therapeutic intervention testing
Cell line retrotransposition reporter assays use a teratocarcinoma line (PA-1) rather than HGSC cells for variant characterization
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid observational genomic study in a rigorously characterized HGSC cohort with multi-technology validation and novel intrapatient heterogeneity insights, fitting Tier 2 (Cancer Discovery / Clinical Cancer Research-caliber) with minor revisions.
